newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo shares hit closing peak, blue chips favoured.
newsitem.headline: Oslo shares hit closing peak, blue chips favoured.

text.p: Norwegian shares raced to new all-time highs on Thursday, buoyed by gains in Europe and demand for blue chip stocks.
Dealers said sentiment remained positive, despite a steep rise in short-term interest rates over the past week.

The Total share index climbed 1.14 percent to end at an all-time peak at 1230.63 points. Turnover was a solid 1.51 billion crowns, with drugs group Nycomed accounting for more than 452 million crowns.
Trade remained heavy in Nycomed and the share price rose after the bourse announced that all the shares issued in the merged Nycomed Amersham group would be used to calculate the All Share Index.
Dealers attributed the rise to expectations that institutional investors would be underweighted in the merged company and would therefore seek to buy stock.
Nycomed A closed four crowns higher at 143 crowns, while the Bs gained three crowns to 135 crowns.
Dealers said stocks in the offshore sector were buoyant despite a profit warning by Transocean Offshore Inc..
